Ivy (Docs): quick heads-up 11 - I'm prepping a small docs PR to unify the Optimize toolkit short-sequence examples (py/js) and add an explicit migration codemod for param renames. Drafting now.

Carlos (Eng): nice. Can you include the exact rename mappings and a tiny sed/perl one-liner codemod? That helps customers and SDK teams.

Vera (ML): also add a compact note about quant_profile safety: q4 profiles are great for throughput but watch for generation quality regressions on certain decoder heads. Recommend evals.

Ivy (Docs): draft mapping in the doc: "batch_size -> micro_batch", "prefetch_kv -> kv_prefetch", "prefetch_cache -> kv_prefetch", "quant_profile -> quant_profile (same) but semantics clarified"

Ben (Product): please add a one-liner for PD customers: if you're on Dedicated with pinned kernels, consult the compatibility matrix before switching q4 profiles.

Ivy (Docs): adding codemod note. Proposed one-liner for bash: `grep -Rnl "batch_size" docs examples | xargs sed -i "s/batch_size/micro_batch/g"` - thoughts?

Carlos (Eng): that's fine as a user example but add a safer perl version that writes backups: `perl -i.bak -pe "s/\bbatch_size\b/micro_batch/g" -0777 -pi` or recommend git-backed changes.

Vera (ML): include sample perf table for readers: micro_batch sizes vs expected latencies for short prompts (median). Keep it approximate.

Ivy (Docs): proposed table (text inline):
- interactive: micro_batch 1-4, kv_prefetch false/true (try true) -> target p50 < 200ms
- conversational: micro_batch 4-12, kv_prefetch true -> p50 200-500ms
- throughput: micro_batch 12+, kv_prefetch true -> p50 > 500ms but higher throughput

Carlos (Eng): add a short CI note: our snippet-tests fail if imports don't match test env (we had flakes earlier). Recommend using `from redwood.optimize import OptimizeClient` in Py examples and `require('@redwood/optimize-client')` in Node.

Ivy (Docs): doing that. Also adding a tiny example Py streaming snippet showing kv prefetch and q4 profile.

Ivy (Docs): snippet for py:
```python
from redwood.optimize import OptimizeClient
c = OptimizeClient()
for chunk in c.stream(model='gpt-like-7b', prompt='TL;DR:', micro_batch=4, kv_prefetch=True, quant_profile='q4_0'):
    print(chunk.text)
```

Vera (ML): good. Add a YAML example for the quant profile so customers can copy/paste in config: 
```yaml
name: q4_0
bits: 4
per_channel: true
fallback: fp16
notes: Prefer A100/T4. Test on your model family.```

Ivy (Docs): adding that and a short eval checklist: small sample set, compute PPL/ROUGE diff, human spot checks.

Ben (Product): can we also call out a tiny UX tweak: in the Optimize Console we'll surface a migration banner for customers who have saved routes using old param names. I'll loop in Console team.

Carlos (Eng): CI reminder: if docs change examples, update examples/tests/requirements.txt to include optimize-client so snippet-tests don't fail. We had a false negative yesterday.

ci-bot: lint started for branch docs/opt-unify-3309 - running snippet-tests, md-lint, link-check.

ci-bot: snippet-tests: failed - examples/js/shortseq.js line 4: ModuleNotFoundError: Cannot find module '@redwood/optimize-client' in test env.

Carlos (Eng): we'll add alias in test matrix, but for the docs change easiest is to update the example to `const { OptimizeClient } = require('@redwood/optimize-client');` (exact). Also include a short note in CONTRIBUTING about matching the harness.

Ivy (Docs): updated JS snippet and added CONTRIBUTING note. Pushing commit.

ci-bot: rerun checks - md-lint warning: long line 112. Shortening.

Ivy (Docs): shortened the long line and added a redirect link for the old qprofiles path which was 404.

ci-bot: All checks passed. PR merged. Deployed to staging docs: https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/optimize/unified-shortseq.

Ben (Product): thanks! I'll add to release notes and ask Console to schedule a small banner for the next release cadence.

Vera (ML): I'll post a short internal note in #eng-ml about the quant_profile caution and link to the new docs.

Ivy (Docs): closing thread. If anyone notices wording that reads too hand-wavy, ping me and I'll tighten. :sparkles:
